pie: kúdʰe h₂éwh₂e mélit widṓmes? ǵr̥h₂n̥tés pr̥kʷéws h₂ewlóy. kʷís mélit péh₂sti? ǵʰwḗres h₁íd ph₂sénti dn̥ḱént-kʷe. tóybʰos bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e. mē tréses. tóns dʰuh₂móh₁ h₂epó h₂éǵomes. nu dlukú mélit léyǵʰsi. mélit h₂mélǵesos swéh₂dyos? h₁íd ǵéwse ǵnéh₃esi-kʷe.
english: Grandfather, where shall we find honey? In the hollow of the old oak. Who guards the honey? Beasts guard it, and they bite. I am afraid of them! Do not tremble! We drive them away with smoke. Then you will lick the sweet honey. Is honey sweeter than milk? Taste it, and you will know.

pie: awis akwāsas ka.
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: kʷíd h₂énHe sweh₂dú? mélit médʰu-kʷe sweh₂dwíh₁. kʷíd piḱróm? h₂eh₃méh₂es wréh₂des piḱréh₂es. kʷóterom lubʰyési? mélit-ge lubʰyóh₂. m̥lités kʷid swéh₂dyos? méh₂tr̥s kéh₂nmn̥ m̥lités swéh₂dyos.
english: Grandmother, what is sweet? Honey and mead are sweet. What is bitter? Raw roots are bitter. Which of the two do you love? I do love honey! Is anything sweeter than honey? A mother's song is sweeter than honey.

pie: pótni gʰósteyes h₂éyeri gʷm̥yétes. kʷíd tóybʰos pékʷōmes? h₂egʷnóm moréye h₁ím-kʷe méǵh₂i kʷéroy h₂réydʰōh₂. h₂ólut h₁ésti? polh₁ú h₂ólut h₁ésti. kʷóti gʷm̥yónti? déḱm̥ wiHrṓs pénkʷe-kʷe gʷénh₂es. nu dwóh₁ h₂egʷnóh₁ moréye.
english: Wife, guests are coming tomorrow. What shall we cook for them? Kill a lamb, and I will prepare it in the big pot. Is there beer? There is much beer. How many are coming? Ten men and five women. Then kill two lambs!

pie: kʷóti h₂ówins súHnew ǵʰiméney moréyes? tísrn̥s h₂ówins h₁óynom-kʷe súHm̥. séh₂omes? séh₂omes h₁yód gʷówes kéh₂ileh₂es h₁ésonti. kʷóti bʰn̥ǵʰéws h₂mélǵesos bʰólǵʰins h₂réydʰes? kʷetwórn̥s bʰólǵʰins. nu ǵʰimés ne bʰebʰih₂mé.
english: Son, how many sheep did you kill for the winter? Three sheep and one pig. Will we be sated? We will be sated, if the cows are healthy. How many bags of thick milk did you prepare? Four bags. Then we do not fear the winter.

pie: bʰréh₂ter h₂éydʰos ne dʰégʷʰeti dṓm-kʷe dʰuh₂móh₁ pl̥h₁nós. dóru ne h₂sowsóm. kʷís ḱód dóru bʰéret? h₂éwh₂os nos h₁íd déh₂nus bʰéret. h₂sowsóm dóru wédʰe h₂éydʰom-kʷe h₂éti h₂éydʰoh₂. h₁íd wédʰom. nu h₂éydʰos dʰégʷʰeti. nu kʷérom h₂éydʰoy h₁épi sodéye.
english: Brother, the fire does not burn, and the house is full of smoke. The wood is not dry. Who brought this wood? Our uncle brought it from the river. Bring dry wood, and I will kindle the fire again. I have brought it. Now the fire is burning! Now set the pot on the fire.

pie: wíHre ḱwṓ ǵʰh₂énsm̥ gʷréws klépet. kúdʰe só drémt? kʷékʷloy Hn̥dʰí légʰeti h₁íh₂m̥ gʷr̥h₃éti. nu séh₂ ǵʰh₂éns tósmey h₁ésti. h₂élyod h₁ésti? káprosyo skélos dʰuh₂móy h₁ésti. skélos bʰr̥ǵyé bʰórm̥-kʷe déms h₁éǵʰs h₂éǵe.
english: Husband, the dog stole the goose from the spit! Where did he run? He is lying under the wagon; he is devouring it. Now that goose belongs to him. Is there something else? There is a goat's leg in the smoke. Roast the leg, and drive the thief out of the house!

pie: "ḱludʰí moi, pter werune!"
english: "Hear me, father Werunos!"

pie: h₂énHe moy wĺ̥kʷosyo spélom wr̥h₁dʰí. kénkonts wĺ̥kʷos dṓm gʷémt. mḗms gʷréwi h₃édet. h₁íd gʷr̥h₃ét? h₁íd ne gʷr̥h₃ét. ḱwṓ h₁ím kʷéḱt h₁ésyo-kʷe h₁orséh₂m dénḱt. wĺ̥kʷos h₂epó drémt. wĺ̥kʷoybʰos bʰebʰóyh₂th₂e? ne bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e dʰr̥sús h₁ésmi.
english: Grandmother, tell me a story about a wolf. A hungry wolf came to a house. He smelled the meat on the spit. Did he devour it? He did not devour it. The dog saw him and bit his tail. The wolf ran away. Are you afraid of wolves? I am not afraid; I am bold.

pie: swéḱruh₂ me ḱHsdʰí. kʷíh₁ bʰn̥ǵʰú h₂mélǵos h₂réydʰesi? gʷṓs h₂éyeri h₂ml̥ǵmés. nu h₁íd h₂Hséh₂i h₁épi dʰedʰh₁més. suHróm bʰuHyéti? suHróm bʰn̥ǵʰú-kʷe bʰuHyéti. h₁íd bʰólǵʰim h₁n̥dó dʰedʰh₁més wódr̥-kʷe h₁éǵʰs sréweti. h₁íd sweh₂dú? h₁íd ne sweh₂dú ǵʰiméni-kʷe nos h₂életi. téwe te méh₂tēr ne ḱéHst? h₁íh₂ me ne ḱéHst h₁ésyeh₂s h₂óweyes péh₂ureh₂es h₁sént.
english: Mother-in-law, teach me! How do you prepare thick milk? In the morning we milk the cows. Then we put it near the hearth. Does it become sour? It becomes sour and thick. We put it into a skin bag, and the water flows out. Is it sweet? It is not sweet, and in winter it nourishes us. Did your mother not teach you? She did not teach me; her sheep were few.

pie: kúdʰe súHnew h₂egʷnós h₁ésti h₁yóm bʰr̥ǵyṓmes? wĺ̥kʷos h₁ím nékʷti sléh₂gʷt. ḱwónes h₂ówins ne ph₂sént? ssént. ph₂trés moy bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e. mē troméyes ǵérh₂ontm̥ káprom pékʷōmes. ǵérh₂onts kápros dʰr̥ǵʰtós.
english: Son, where is the lamb that we will roast? A wolf seized it in the night. Did the dogs not guard the sheep? They were sleeping. I fear my father. Do not tremble; we will cook the old goat. The old goat is hard!

pie: méh₂ter albʰéh₂ gʷṓws h₂mélǵos ne dédeh₃ti. h₁íh₂m̥ h₂éyeri h₂mélǵs? h₁íh₂m̥ h₂mélǵm̥ péh₂urom dédeh₃t. h₁ésyeh₂s wetsós h₁íd píph₃eti. wetsóm h₁ésyeh₂s h₂epó wédʰe. nu wetsós HréwdHti. HréwdHtu wékʷsperoy h₂éti srobʰéyeti.
english: Mother, the white cow does not give milk. Did you milk her this morning? I milked her, but she gave little. Her calf is drinking it. Lead the calf away from her. Then the calf will bellow. Let it bellow; in the evening it will suck again.

pie: kʷíd h₂mélǵos h₂éydʰom h₁n̥dó ǵʰéws? sh₂krós h₁n̥gʷnís h₁íd deywóns bʰéreti. h₁yód deywṓs péh₃onti nu píph₃omes. deywṓs nos widéh₁yonti? widéh₁yonti nos gʷṓs-kʷe nos h₂ówins-kʷe dedh₃wós. nu moy h₁n̥gʷnéyey bʰoh₂góm éti déh₃oh₂. h₁ím h₂éydʰom h₁n̥dó Hih₁kdʰí h₁ím-kʷe gʷr̥nHdʰí.
english: Why did you pour milk into the fire? Holy Fire carries it to the gods. When the gods have drunk, then we drink. Do the gods see us? They see us, and they give us cows and sheep. Then I too will give my portion to Fire. Throw it into the fire, and praise him!

pie: swésor toy h₂ébolm̥ ḱéstroh₁ bʰinddʰí. h₁ím bʰéydm̥. kʷóterom wéḱsi? méǵh₂m̥. nu péh₂urom sléh₂gʷoh₂ méǵh₂s suHrós. nu moy péh₂urom dh₃dʰí. wélh₁s méǵh₂m̥ h₂ḱh₃dʰí.
english: Sister, split the apple with your knife! I have split it. Which of the two do you want? The big one. Then I will take the small one; but the big one is sour! Then give me the small one! You chose; eat the big one!

pie: pékʷtor moy wéwke kʷíh₁ mḗms bʰólǵʰēy pékʷesi? h₂éḱmonn̥s ph₂wéni topéyonti. gʷʰermóns h₂éḱmonn̥s wódr̥ h₁n̥dó Hyéh₁km̥ yéseti-kʷe. skéwHtis ne dʰégʷʰeti? ne dʰégʷʰeti h₂ékʷeh₂ h₁íh₂m̥ péh₂sti. mḗms ǵéwse h₁íd ml̥dú? h₁íd ml̥dú dlukú-kʷe. túH ǵn̥h₃rós pékʷtōr.
english: Tell me, cook: how do you cook meat in a skin bag? I heat stones in the fire. I throw the hot stones into the water, and it boils. Does the skin not burn? It does not burn; the water guards it. Taste the meat: is it soft? It is soft and sweet. You are a wise cook.

pie: gʷḗn tr̥syóh₂. h₂ékʷeh₂m moy dh₃dʰí. h₂mélǵos ph₃dʰí h₁íd gʷʰermóm. h₁íd dlukú. térpm̥. kúdʰe h₁éysi? h₃rēǵés ḱóymom h₁éymi. h₂sowsóm ḱóm skʷálom sl̥h₂gʷdʰí. ḱéyweh₂ moy h₁ési deywṓs toy h₁wésuh₂ dh₃ih₁ént.
english: Woman, I am thirsty. Give me water. Drink milk; it is warm. It is sweet. I am sated. Where are you going? I am going to the king's village. Take this dried fish. You are dear to me; may the gods give you good things.

pie: kʷíd wóyḱe séh₂lm̥ mémsi h₁épi dʰédʰeh₁si? ǵʰéymn̥ gʷm̥yéti. sḗh₂l h₁íd péh₂sti ne-kʷe púHyeti. nu kʷíd dʰédʰeh₁si? h₁íd dʰuh₂móy h₂Hséh₂i upér dʰédʰeh₁mi. dʰuh₂mós h₁íd h₂sowséyeti. kʷóm h₂susyéti? h₂susyéti h₁yód snóygʷʰos séngʷeti. h₃éngʷn̥ toy démi h₁ésti? ne kʷid h₁ésti. bʰréh₂tēr moy pérunsu h₂éyeri wrégeti.
english: Neighbour, why do you put salt on the meat? Winter is coming. Salt guards it, and it does not rot. What do you do then? I put it in the smoke over the hearth. The smoke dries it. When will it be dry? It will be dry when the snow falls. Is there fat in your house? There is nothing. Tomorrow my brother hunts in the mountains.

pie: stéh₂dʰh₁oybʰos pérwōr h₂éǵoh₂. h₂sowsóm skʷálom h₂élbʰit-kʷe h₁áyso. kʷóm h₂éti gʷémesi? sh₁séni h₂éti gʷémoh₂. gʷṓs h₂én h₂ml̥ǵdʰí h₂eh₃mā́s-kʷe wréh₂dn̥s mē bʰés. skʷálom h₂éydʰoy topéyoh₂. súHnew moy te dyḗws ph₂syéh₁t.
english: I am driving the herd to the mountains. Take dried fish and barley. When will you come back? I will come back in autumn. Milk the cows there, and do not chew raw roots! I will heat the fish on the fire. May Dyēus protect you, my son.

pie: ǵérh₂ont gʷówes ḱósmi méh₁nsi mh₂ḱréh₂es. téḱneh₂ kénketi dʰoHnéh₂-kʷe lelóykʷe. polh₁úns mh₂ḱróns méh₁nsn̥s dedórḱh₂e. sémeh₂ h₂éti gʷm̥yéti. nu kʷíd téḱnoybʰos dédeh₃omes? gʷĺ̥h₂nons wréh₂dn̥s-kʷe drúsu léǵe diwéy-kʷe gʷʰédʰye. nu h₁éymi.
english: Elder, the cows are lean this month. The children are hungry, and the grain is gone. I have seen many lean months. Summer will come again. What shall we give the children now? Gather acorns and roots among the trees, and pray to Dyēus. I will go now.

pie: h₃rḗḱs súHnum wl̥nh₁to.
english: The king wanted a son.

pie: h₂énHe yéwHs ǵéwse h₁yód h₂réydʰom. h₁íd ǵéwsm̥ sḗh₂l h₁ésmōd lelóykʷe. séh₂lm̥ dʰéh₁oh₂? séh₂lm̥ dʰh₁dʰí wósh₂r̥-kʷe miḱdʰí. nu swéh₂deti. kʷís te ḱéHst? méne me h₂énHos ḱéHst ḱéHsoh₂-kʷe te.
english: Grandmother, taste the broth that I prepared. I have tasted it; salt is missing from it. Shall I put in salt? Put in salt, and mix in garlic. Then it will become tasty. Who taught you? My grandmother taught me, and I will teach you.

pie: h₂éti gʷegʷómth₂e. kʷíd moréyes? h₂ŕ̥tḱom. bʰréh₂teres moy h₁ím dṓm bʰéronti. h₂ŕ̥tḱos sph₁rós. h₁ésyo nos skéwHtis ǵʰyémi stégeti h₁ésyo-kʷe sélpos tinh₁més. h₂ŕ̥tḱos te ne dénḱt? skélos moy dénḱt kéh₂ilos h₁ésmi.
english: You have come back! What did you kill? A bear. My brothers are carrying it home. The bear is fat! Its skin will cover us in winter, and we will melt its fat. Did the bear not bite you? It bit my leg, but I am whole.

pie: gʷḗn toy wékʷesh₂ ne ǵn̥néh₃mi. kʷíh₁ mléwHmi? kénkoh₂. kénkoh₂. dʰugh₂tréy moy tód wéwke mā́dsom-kʷe toy dédeh₃ti. kʷíh₁ mléwHmi? wódr̥ moy dh₃dʰí. wódr̥ moy dh₃dʰí. moḱs h₁éwks. ḱéyweh₂ moy h₁ési.
english: Woman, I do not know your words. How do I say it? I am hungry. I am hungry. Say that to my daughter, and she will give you food. And how do I say it? Give me water. Give me water. You learn quickly. You are dear to me.

pie: kʷíd h₂éwh₂e m̥dʰéwi h₁ésti? mélit wódr̥-kʷe. h₁íh₂ miḱsḱóh₂ h₁íh₂-kʷe h₂Hséh₂i h₁épi dʰédʰeh₁mi médʰu-kʷe Hwérdʰt. h₁íd péh₃oh₂? túH h₂yuHn̥ḱós médʰu wiHróybʰos h₁ésti. yéwHs píph₃e. kʷóm wiHrós bʰúHoh₂? h₁yód h₂wéksesi médʰu méǵʰye ḱóm péh₃esi.
english: Uncle, what is in mead? Honey and water. I mix them, and I put them by the hearth, and the mead becomes strong. Shall I drink it? You are young; mead is for men. Drink broth! When will I become a man? When you have grown up, you will drink mead with me.

pie: kʷíh₁ príHe pkʷtréy mléwHmi? ǵʰh₂éns sph₁réh₂. ǵʰh₂éns sph₁réh₂. pkʷtréy tód wéwke méwdeti-kʷe. kʷíh₁ mléwHmi? h₂élyod moy h₂éluts péh₃tlom dh₃dʰí. h₂élyod moy h₂éluts péh₃tlom dh₃dʰí. pénkʷe péh₃tleh₂ mē píph₃es. h₁óynom píph₃ōh₂.
english: Friend, how do I say it to the cook? The goose is fat. The goose is fat. Say that to the cook, and he will rejoice. And how do I say it? Give me another cup of beer. Give me another cup of beer. But do not drink five cups! I will drink one.

pie: kʷóm h₂éwh₂e súHm̥ moréyōmes? h₁ím sh₁séni moréyomes h₁yód sph₁rós h₁ésti. kʷíd h₁ḗdti? gʷĺ̥h₂nons. súHm̥ pérkʷuns Hn̥dʰí h₂éyeri h₁l̥h₂dʰí. h₁ésyo nos sélpos ǵʰiméni h₂életi? h₂életi nos gʷʰréh₁yomes-kʷe.
english: Uncle, when will we kill the pig? We kill it in autumn, when it is fat. What does it eat? Acorns. Drive the pig under the oaks tomorrow. Will its fat nourish us in winter? It will nourish us, and we will be warm.

pie: ḱóm mā́dsom ne wéḱmi. kʷíd moy téḱnom h₁ím ne wéḱsi? h₁éy piḱrós. h₁éy ne piḱrós mélit h₁ím h₁n̥dó dʰéh₁m̥. h₁ím ǵéwse. h₁ím ǵéwsm̥. h₁éy sweh₂dús. h₂élyom moy bʰoh₂góm dh₃dʰí. ḱóm h₂ḱh₃dʰí nu toy h₂élyom h₁opéyoh₂.
english: I do not want this mush. Why do you not want it, my child? It is bitter. It is not bitter; I put honey into it. Taste it! I have tasted it. It is sweet! Give me another portion! Eat up this one; then I give you another.

pie: kʷíd ph₂ter ne h₁ḗdsi? dʰúgh₂ter moy h₃dóntes lelikʷḗr. mḗms moy dʰr̥ǵʰtéh₂. nu toy ml̥dúm mā́dsom h₃n̥gʷénh₁ h₂réydʰōh₂. túH h₁uséwih₂ dʰugh₂tḗr. bʰréh₂teres toy h₂ḱh₃ént? h₂ḱh₃ént h₂éǵrom-kʷe gʷh₂ént.
english: Father, why do you not eat? My teeth are gone, daughter. The meat is hard for me. Then I will prepare soft mush with butter for you. You are a good daughter. Did your brothers eat? They ate, and they went to the field.
